If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast slope in mid-horizon by 10–15% to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently bearish (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast slope in early horizon by 10–15% to compensate for downward momentum.  
When sentiment swings from bullish to bearish within 5 days, shift forecast peak to later horizon (≥day 15) and reduce amplitude by 15–20%.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) across 5+ days, apply linear smoothing to forecast path to reduce volatility in mid-to-late horizon.  
If forecast consistently exceeds true value by >5% in early horizon, apply downward bias correction starting from day 7, reducing by 2–3% per day.  
If true price shows sharp upward breakout after sentiment shift to bullish, extend forecast peak to day 18+ and add 5–8% upward momentum buffer.
